==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈtɛm.pl̩/}}, {{enPR|tĕm'pl}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-temple.ogg|a=UK}} * {{audio|en|En-us-temple.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/tɪm.pl̩/|[ˈtɪm.pl̩]|a=US,pin-pen}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛmpəl|s=2}} * {{hmp|en|timple|aa1=pin-pen}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*temh₁-}} {{wp}} [[File:Philae temple at night.jpg|thumb|right|The Temple of Isis in Philae (Egypt)]] [[File:Maison Carree in Nimes (16).jpg|thumb|right|Maison Carrée in Nîmes (France), one of the best preserved Roman temples to survive in the territory of the former Roman Empire]] [[File:Ryusenji-Temple01.JPG|thumb|right|Ryusenji temple in Osaka (Japan)]] From {{inh|en|enm|temple}}, from {{inh|en|ang|templ}}, {{m|ang|tempel}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|templum||shrine, temple, area for auspices}}. Compare {{noncog|goh|tempal|t=temple}}, also a borrowing from the Latin. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|ealh}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q44539}}A [[house of worship]], [[especially]]: ## A [[house of worship]] [[dedicate]]d to a [[polytheistic]] [[faith]]. ##: {{ux|en|The '''temple''' of Zeus was very large.}} ##* {{quote-book |en |year=1974 |author=Donald R. DeGlopper |chapter=Religion and Ritual in Lukang |editor=Arthur P. Wolf |title=Religion and Ritual in Chinese Society |series=Studies in Chinese Society |url=https://archive.org/details/religionritualin0000unse/ |location=[[Stanford]] |publisher=w:Stanford University Press |ISBN=0-8047-0858-4 |LCCN=73-89863 |OCLC=844556505 |page=46 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/religionritualin0000unse/page/46/ |text=As of October 1968 Lukang, which had a resident population of between 27,000 and 28,000 people, had 39 '''temples'''. It is my impression that Lukang has more '''temples''' than do most Taiwanese communities of equivalent size. By '''temple''' I mean a structure that houses an image, altar, and incense pot, and is freely accessible to the general public. In speaking of the 39 '''temples''' of Lukang, I am omitting the numerous small shrines to the unknown dead (Yu Ying Kung), buildings dedicated to ancestors rather than deities (two), Christian churches (four), incense-burner associations that keep their incense pot or image in private homes, and private shrines such as the domestic altars of ''tang-ki'' (spirit mediums) or the shrine of the now defunct Ch'üan-chou guild, found in the back room of a drugstore endowed with the guild property.[...]Lukang, seen in comparative perspective, has a lot of '''temples'''.}} ## {{lb|en|Judaism}} {{syn of|en|synagogue}}, [[especially]] a [[non-]][[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox]] [[synagogue]]. ##: ''How often do you go to '''temple'''?'' ## {{lb|en|Mormonism}} As opposed to an LDS meetinghouse, a [[church]] [[close]]d to [[non-]][[Mormon]]s and [[necessary]] for [[particular]] [[ritual]]s. # A [[meeting]] [[house]] of the [[Oddfellow]]s [[fraternity]]; its [[member]]s. # {{lb|en|figurative}} Any [[place]] [[regard]]ed as [[hold]]ing a [[religious]] [[presence]]. # {{lb|en|figurative}} Any place seen as an important centre for some activity. #: {{ux|en|a '''temple''' of commerce''; ''a '''temple''' of drinking and dining}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} [[anything|Anything]] [[regard]]ed as [[important]] or [[minutely]] [[cared for]]. #: {{ux|en|My body is my '''temple'''.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|1|3|lines=11–14|text=For nature crescent does not grow alone
In thews and bulks, but as this '''temple''' waxes,
The inward service of the mind and soul
Grows wide withal.}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[gesture]] wherein the [[forefinger]]s are [[outstretched]] and [[touch]] [[fingerpad|pad]] to pad while the [[other]] [[finger]]s are [[clasp]]ed [[together]]. =====Usage notes===== * This word is rarely used in English to refer to a Christian house of worship, especially in Western Christianity. =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|house of worship}} {{l|en|house of worship}}, {{l|en|place of worship}} =====Hyponyms===== * {{sense|house of worship}} {{l|en|church}} {{qualifier|Christian, usually distinguished}}; {{l|en|mosque}} {{qualifier|Muslim, Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=219|passage=Biblical criteria of sexual seductiveness include a white skin, black hair, or henna-dyed, scarlet lips, a prominent nose, rosy '''temples''', long straight neck, firm breasts, round thighs, an erect posture.}} #* {{RQ:en:National Public Radio|title=Epilepsy Patients Help Decode The Brain's Hidden Signals|author=Amy Standen|date=Dec 9 2013 |text=A few days after the electrodes were implanted, Bennett welcomed visitors into his hospital room.
